subject: Q3 readiness: customer health synopsis + renewal triage (exec prioritization)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Q3 readiness: Nova Analytics health snapshot + renewal triage (need exec asks)

Team —

I'm pulling together the QBR prep materials for Nova Analytics (renewal due 2026-09-30). Quick synopsis attached; main items for leadership attention below.

Summary highlights
- Usage: 18% QoQ token volume decline tied to last-month model throttling incident (we patched, customer still testing).
- Costs: customer is within committed spend but growth has slowed; they're evaluating a 1-year renewal with tighter T&Cs.
- Open support items: two P1 escalations resolved, one outstanding API rate-limit anomaly flagged by their infra team.

Top renewal risks (see renewal-triage workbook attached)
1) Perceived instability: incident history + recent throttling risk leading to price pushback.
2) SLA/latency demands: Nova is asking for a 99.9% latency SLO for a narrow set of endpoints — this will require non-trivial capacity reservation.
3) Commercial: procurement pushing for a 20% discount and extended payment terms.

Proposed exec asks (what we need from GTM/Finance/CEO):
- Approve a one-time goodwill credit of up to $45k tied to incident impact (to be applied as account credit, contingent on customer signing a 12-month renewal).
- Provide authority for a capped committed-capacity offer to meet the 99.9% SLO for their core endpoints (we can scope exact GPU commitment after alignment).
- Allow Sales to entertain net-30 payment terms for existing MRR if we secure the 12-month term.

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Lauren: finalize updated ARR and adjusted unit economics for the proposed credits (needed by EOD 8/10).
- Jordan: draft a short exec-facing one-pager with recommended decision matrix and fallback options (target 8/11 morning).
- I'll coordinate a prep call with the customer and include the above asks.

Attachments: nova-health-snapshot-2026-08.pdf, renewal-triage-DN-3482.xlsx, qbr-prep-ask-list.docx

Thanks — Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success (Midmarket)
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Date: 2026-08-10T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Q3 readiness: Nova Analytics health snapshot + renewal triage (need exec asks)

Thanks Grace — reviewed the snapshot and workbook. A few quick items:

- I've attached a short ARR bridge in the renewal-triage workbook (tab 'ARR-impact'). If we offer the $45k credit the net present value of the deal drops ~8% unless we tighten committed capacity.
- Confirming the customer's request: they want the 99.9% latency SLO applied to two inference endpoints that together represent ~62% of their token volume. Achieving that reliably will likely require reserved capacity or priority lanes.

Action: I'll push a revised numbers tab and stress-tested cost scenarios by EOD 8/10. I recommend the exec one-pager include: (1) credit amount & conditions, (2) capacity delta (GPUs/hour), (3) fallback (reduced SLO or graduated ramp).

Attachment: renewal-triage-DN-3482.xlsx (updated: ARR-impact tab)

-Lauren

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Q3 readiness: Nova Analytics health snapshot + renewal triage (need exec asks)

Quick read — I support the conditional credit but suggest we structure it as a milestone credit (e.g., 50% on signature, 50% after 60 days with no production incidents). Also:

- Recommend we include an 'operational runway' clause that lets us scale the SLO commitment incrementally over 3 months to avoid upfront capacity commitment risk.
- I'll draft the exec one-pager and include two clear decision asks: (A) approve credit ceiling, (B) approve pilot capacity reservation authorization up to X GPUs for 90 days.

I'll have the one-pager in your inbox by 11:00 PT 8/11.

-Jordan
